_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mauritius covering uninhabited discovery, Dutch/French/British colonial periods, sugar plantations, Indian indentured labour, dodo extinction, independence, and economic miracle (Africa's highest HDI).

910.name: Uninhabited Island and Early Sightings
910.description: Volcanic island in the Indian Ocean; no indigenous human population; Arab and Portuguese sailors sight the island before Dutch arrival.

sub_clusters.name: Volcanic Formation and Endemic Species
sub_clusters.description: Mauritius formed by volcanic activity ~10 million years ago; evolution of unique endemic species including the dodo, giant tortoises, and native flora.

sub_clusters.name: Arab and Portuguese Sightings
sub_clusters.description: Arab navigators possibly map the island (Dina Arobi); Portuguese chart it as Cerne (c. 1507); no permanent settlement established.

920.name: Dutch Colonial Period
920.description: Dutch East India Company names island after Prince Maurits; ebony exploitation; introduction of sugar cane; dodo driven to extinction; Dutch abandon island.

sub_clusters.name: Dutch Settlement and Exploitation
sub_clusters.description: Admiral Wybrand van Warwyck claims island 1598; named Mauritius after Prince Maurits of Nassau; ebony forests logged; enslaved workers from Madagascar.

sub_clusters.name: Extinction of the Dodo
sub_clusters.description: Flightless dodo (Raphus cucullatus) driven to extinction by hunting, introduced predators, and habitat destruction; last sighting c. 1681.

sub_clusters.name: Dutch Abandonment
sub_clusters.description: Two periods of Dutch occupation; cyclones, droughts, and pest damage; Dutch permanently abandon Mauritius 1710.

930.name: French Colonial Period (Île de France)
930.description: France colonises island as Île de France; sugar plantation economy; slave-based labour; corsair base; Mahé de La Bourdonnais as governor.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation of Île de France
sub_clusters.description: French East India Company claims island 1715; renamed Île de France; Mahé de La Bourdonnais as governor from 1735 transforms the colony.

sub_clusters.name: Sugar Plantations and Slavery
sub_clusters.description: Sugar cane becomes dominant crop; enslaved people from East Africa, Madagascar, and India; code noir; Maroon communities.

sub_clusters.name: Corsair Base and Napoleonic Wars
sub_clusters.description: Île de France as base for French corsairs (Surcouf) raiding British Indian Ocean shipping; British capture the island after Battle of Grand Port 1810.

940.name: British Colonial Mauritius
940.description: British capture and Treaty of Paris; abolition of slavery; Indian indentured labour transforms demographics; sugar monoculture; path to independence.

sub_clusters.name: British Takeover and Abolition
sub_clusters.description: Britain captures Mauritius 1810; Treaty of Paris 1814; French laws and language retained; abolition of slavery 1835; apprenticeship system.

sub_clusters.name: Indian Indentured Labour System
sub_clusters.description: Over 450,000 Indian indentured labourers brought to sugar plantations (Aapravasi Ghat, UNESCO site); transforms ethnic composition; 'coolie trade' abuses.

sub_clusters.name: Sugar Monoculture Economy
sub_clusters.description: Sugar dominates economy; Franco-Mauritian planter elite; cyclone and malaria challenges; gradual Indian landownership.

sub_clusters.name: Labour Movement and Political Awakening
sub_clusters.description: 1937 labour unrest; Mauritius Labour Party founded; Seewoosagur Ramgoolam; universal suffrage 1959; Lancaster House conferences.

950.name: Independence and Nation-Building
950.description: Independence 1968 amid ethnic tensions; Chagos Archipelago detached; Ramgoolam and Jugnauth era; economic diversification begins.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Mauritius
sub_clusters.description: Independence 12 March 1968; Seewoosagur Ramgoolam as first PM; ethnic riots precede independence; Chagos Archipelago (incl. Diego Garcia) detached by Britain.

sub_clusters.name: Chagos Archipelago Detachment
sub_clusters.description: Britain separates Chagos from Mauritius 1965 (BIOT); Chagossian population expelled for Diego Garcia US base; ICJ 2019 advisory opinion supports Mauritius sovereignty.

sub_clusters.name: Early Economic Diversification
sub_clusters.description: Export Processing Zone (EPZ) established 1971; textiles and manufacturing; Anerood Jugnauth PM; beginning of Mauritian economic miracle.

960.name: Mauritian Economic Miracle
960.description: Republic since 1992; transformation into financial services, ICT, and tourism hub; highest HDI in Africa; multicultural democracy.

sub_clusters.name: Republic of Mauritius
sub_clusters.description: Mauritius becomes a republic within the Commonwealth 1992; Cassam Uteem as first president; parliamentary democracy continues.

sub_clusters.name: Financial Services and ICT Hub
sub_clusters.description: Global Business Licence regime; Mauritius as India-Africa investment gateway; Cybercity Ebène; diversified services economy.

sub_clusters.name: Africa's Highest HDI Achievement
sub_clusters.description: Free healthcare and education; multi-ethnic harmony model; highest Human Development Index in Africa; tourism (1.4M+ visitors); environmental challenges including coral bleaching.

sub_clusters.name: MV Wakashio Oil Spill 2020
sub_clusters.description: Japanese bulk carrier MV Wakashio runs aground July 2020; 1,000 tonnes of oil spill in pristine lagoons; environmental disaster; citizen-led cleanup.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
